newsitem.title: USA: Phillips replaced 71 pct of 1996 production.
newsitem.headline: Phillips replaced 71 pct of 1996 production.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co Wednesday said it replaced 71 percent of its 1996 worldwide hydrocarbon production at an average finding-and-development cost of $7.52 per barrel-of-oil equivalent, or BOE.
From 1992 through 1996, Phillips' five-year-average production replacement equaled 118 percent, while finding-and-development costs averaged $3.79 per BOE.
The company defined finding-and-development costs as the costs of acquiring, exploring for and developing oil and gas reserves, divided by the company's reserve additions.

"While our 1996 results were not as good as in previous years, our long-term performance continues to be one of the best in the industry," said Knut Am, senior vice president, exploration and production. "We expect our outstanding long-term performance to continue."
The firm's worldwide hydrocarbon production in 1996 was up one percent to 189.3 million BOE. This consisted of a 2.2 percent decrease in oil production and a 3.5 percent increase in gas production.

On a BOE basis, Phillips' worldwide proved reserves in 1996 decreased by two percent to 2.15 billion BOE. Worldwide proved reserves of crude oil and condensate remained unchanged, while worldwide proved reserves of natural gas decreased five percent.

Phillips replaced 41 percent of its reserves produced in the United States at an average cost of $6.20 per BOE, while replacing 106 percent of the non-U.S. reserves it produced at an average cost of $8.31 per BOE.
Natural gas comprises 49 percent of proved hydrocarbon reserves worldwide, and 63 percent of U.S. reserves, the company said.
